blueprint.competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts

claim_audit.phenotype: MedlinePlus Description and NCBI Pathophysiology support recurrent hemoglobinuria and thrombosis; NCBI specifically supports intra-abdominal/hepatic venous thrombosis.
claim_audit.flow_cytometry: NCBI Evaluation identifies flow cytometry of GPI-anchored proteins including CD55/CD59 as the gold-standard diagnostic approach.
claim_audit.correct_mechanism: MedlinePlus Causes and NCBI Etiology directly support somatic PIGA mutation, defective GPI anchoring, loss of CD55/CD59, and complement-mediated hemolysis.
claim_audit.distractor_1: NCBI Hereditary Spherocytosis supports membrane/cytoskeletal protein defects including spectrin.
claim_audit.distractor_2: NCBI G6PD Deficiency supports impaired NADPH/redox defense and oxidative hemolysis.
claim_audit.distractor_3: NCBI immune hemolytic anemia review supports warm IgG-mediated RBC destruction.
claim_audit.distractor_4: NCBI TTP supports acquired ADAMTS13 inhibition and microangiopathic thrombosis/hemolysis.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Loss of both CD55 and CD59 on a clonal blood-cell population localizes the defect to GPI anchoring; PNH plus hemoglobinuria and hepatic-vein thrombosis makes a somatic PIGA lesion the single best explanation.
adversarial_second_pass.alternative_mechanisms: The four distractors can cause anemia or thrombosis but none causes clonal loss of GPI-anchored CD55/CD59.
adversarial_second_pass.inherited_vs_acquired: The item asks about typical PNH and the sources explicitly identify the usual lesion as a somatic, acquired PIGA mutation; no family-history assumption is needed.
